prompt.context: Your client, Maxicure, manufactures and sells an over-the-counter cough and cold medicine. Their sole plant in Kentucky is aging, and its increasing maintenance costs are leading to low margins on their products.
prompt.question: How would you advise Maxicure proceed to solve this problem?

clarifying_info.q: How many competitors does Maxicure have?
clarifying_info.a: There are 2-3 larger players in this over-the-counter business who have distribution across the country. Maxicure is one of them.

clarifying_info.q: Where does Maxicure sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: Maxicure sells all of its products in the US.
The objective is to reduce production costs while maintaining product quality. Cost, quality, and brand image all matter to customers.

framework: Option 1: Refurbish the existing Kentucky plant
Option 2: Rebuild on the same site in Kentucky
Option 3: Rebuild at a new location
Option 4: Outsource manufacturing to a third party

Evaluation criteria: Investment cost, new per-unit cost, financial and non-financial benefits, effect on product quality, opportunity to improve technology and capacity, proximity to distribution centers

questions.prompt: What options does Maxicure have for tackling this problem, and what factors would you consider in deciding which option to choose?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify the four main options (refurbish, rebuild same site, rebuild new location, outsource) and evaluate them across dimensions such as investment cost, per-unit cost, quality impact, technology/capacity improvements, and proximity to distribution centers. Many frameworks are acceptable so long as they are MECE and cover financial and operational considerations.

questions.prompt: Maxicure has narrowed down its decision to two options: (1) build a new facility next to the old plant, or (2) outsource manufacturing to a competitor. With the information below, how many bottles of medicine would Maxicure need to sell for the in-house option to be more profitable than the outsourcing option? Data: Selling price per bottle $4.50; In-house initial investment $50M, total cost per bottle $2.00; Outsource total cost per bottle $2.25 for the first 20M bottles and $2.50 for bottles beyond the first 20M (regardless of total order size).
questions.guidance: Candidate should set up a break-even equation where in-house cumulative profit equals outsource cumulative profit. Key insight: the outsource margin changes at 20M units, so the equation must account for that step-change. After solving, push the candidate to select an option and provide supporting reasons.

math.setup: Let x = total bottles sold. In-house profit = 2.50x - 50,000,000. Outsource profit = 2.25 * 20,000,000 + 2.00 * (x - 20,000,000) for x > 20M. Set in-house profit equal to outsource profit and solve for x.

questions.prompt: Maxicure has decided to build a new production facility in Indiana instead of Kentucky to be closer to a major distribution center. How should it convince the governor of Indiana to offer the necessary tax breaks to make the move more profitable?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm arguments appealing to the governor's political and economic incentives. Strong answers cover multiple stakeholder angles. Examples: increased state tax revenue stimulating the economy, job creation for residents, positive press for the governor, attracting other manufacturers to the state, community-building initiatives such as building schools and parks.

brainstorming.prompt: How should Maxicure convince the governor of Indiana to offer tax breaks?

categories.name: Economic benefits to the state
ideas: Increased tax revenue from corporate and employee income taxes
Stimulation of local economy through wages and supplier spend
Attraction of additional manufacturers and related businesses

categories.name: Political benefits to the governor
ideas: Positive press coverage and public image boost
Job creation talking points for re-election
Being seen as pro-business and pro-growth

categories.name: Community benefits
ideas: Building or funding schools and parks as part of the deal
Infrastructure improvements in the surrounding area
Supporting local small businesses through supply chain

recommendation: Maxicure should build a new production facility in Indiana near the major distribution center
Building in-house is preferred over outsourcing if projected volumes exceed 110 million bottles, which should be validated against current and forecast demand
risks: Construction delays or cost overruns on the new facility
Demand may not reach 110 million bottles, making outsourcing more economical
Loss of institutional knowledge or operational continuity during transition
Governor negotiations may fail or tax breaks may not cover the expected benefit
next_steps: Validate volume forecasts against the 110M bottle break-even threshold
Negotiate tax incentives with the Indiana governor
Develop a transition plan to minimize production disruption during the move
Conduct a site selection and logistics analysis to confirm proximity advantage of Indiana location
